annotations.title: Build a portfolio from construction rules

description: Builds a custom portfolio of US listed ETFs from construction choices about the PORTFOLIO, and shows the rule it applied. TWO FORMS. Weights (ETFIQ custom construction rule, version 2): pass weights, the user's own percent for each asset class, adding to exactly 100, for example {"us-stocks": 40, "international-stocks": 15, "us-bonds": 25, "gold": 10, "reits": 10}. The asset classes: us-stocks, us-small-stocks, international-stocks (broad, market-cap-weighted index funds only), international-dividend-stocks, international-esg-stocks, international-factor-stocks, international-ipo-stocks (each only when the user asks for that tilt), emerging-markets-stocks, reits, us-bonds (core, intermediate), us-bonds-short, us-bonds-long, us-corporate-bonds, government-bonds-short, government-bonds-intermediate, government-bonds-long, tips, high-yield-bonds, cash (Treasury bills), gold, commodities (broad), alternatives. Defaults: cheapest funds, one fund per asset class, no fee ceiling; the answer's defaults.line names the ones used. Band (version 1): pass band, include and funds, and the rule sets the weights (stocks at the band's point, international, broad market-cap-weighted funds only, 40% of stocks outside themes, themes 10% of stocks, commodities and alternatives 5% each from bonds, US bonds the rest). In each asset class or sleeve the cheapest (or largest) funds that file N-PORT (a gold trust: its 10-Q or 10-K), hold at least $100 million and have three years of prices, each fund's fee with its filing date. WHEN THE USER GIVES WEIGHTS, call the weights form at once, mapping their words to the ids above; ask at most ONE follow-up, and only for what has no default: weights that do not add to 100 (kind weights-total), or an asset class with no id here (kind unknown-class). When the user gives neither weights nor a band, ask once for one of them; the bands by stock share are conservative: more than 15% and up to 30% stocks; moderately-conservative: more than 30% and up to 50%; moderate: more than 50% and up to 70%; moderately-aggressive: more than 70% and up to 85%; aggressive: more than 85%. NEVER ask about, and never pass, the person's age, income, savings, net worth, goals, time horizon, tax situation, risk tolerance, employment or family, and never turn what someone says about themselves into weights or a band: those are the user's choices about the portfolio. If asked whether a portfolio suits someone, or whether to buy or sell it, say that ETFIQ does not answer that and give the not-advice line. Its returns field carries the portfolio's hypothetical returns (ETFIQ custom rule, version 3: the weights reset at every month end, as the ETFIQ benchmarks are): total return, return a year, volatility and month-end drawdown over 1Y, 3Y, 5Y, 10Y and since the first month end all its funds share, a window given only where every fund has prices across it; returns.common.sentence says where the history starts and why. Show them as hypothetical, never extend a window, and never estimate a return the answer does not give. To set the portfolio beside an ETFIQ benchmark, call compare_to_benchmark with the answer's compare.arguments. Every response carries the not-advice line in not_advice: show it with the portfolio.

band.description: Version 1: the stock-share band the portfolio should sit in.

feeCeiling.description: The most any one fund may charge, in percent a year (0.25 is 0.25%).

funds.description: How many funds: 2 to 12 with a band; with weights, at least one per asset class (the default).

themeIds.description: Theme ids, only when themes is true.

weights.description: Version 2: the user's own percent of the portfolio for each asset class, adding to 100.
